hints.content:
### Definition of tangent

For an angle with measure $\theta$ in a right triangle:

$\tan(\theta)=\dfrac{\blueE{\text{opposite leg length}}}{\goldE{\text{adjacent leg length}}}$

### Identifying the sides opposite and adjacent to $\angle A$

The side $\blueE{\text{opposite}}$ to $\angle A$ is $\overline{BC}$ and its length is $\blueE{35}$ units.

The side $\goldE{\text{adjacent}}$ to $\angle A$ is $\overline{AC}$ and its length is $\goldE{12}$ units.

This is the side *adjacent* to $\angle A$ divided by the side *opposite* to $\angle A$.

But $\tan(\alpha)$ is the side *opposite* to $\angle A$ divided by the side *adjacent* to $\angle A$.

This is the side opposite to $\angle A$ divided by the *hypotenuse*.

But $\tan(\alpha)$ is the side opposite to $\angle A$ divided by the side *adjacent* to $\angle A$.

This is the side *adjacent* to $\angle A$ divided by the *hypotenuse*.

But $\tan(\alpha)$ is the side *opposite* to $\angle A$ divided by the side *adjacent* to $\angle A$.
